title: NAND Universal Logic Gate (IC 7400)
summary: A NAND gate (NOT-AND) is a universal logic gate that produces a LOW (0) output IF AND ONLY IF all inputs are HIGH (1). It can synthesize any Boolean function without requiring other gate types.

working_principle: The NAND gate combines an AND gate followed by an Inverter. When inputs A and B are both +5V, the output is 0V. For all other input combinations (00, 01, 10), the output is +5V.
applications: Universal Logic Synthesis in Digital IC Design
SR Flip-Flop Latches and Memory Registers
Active-Low Decoding and Bus Line Control
advantages: Universal Gate: Can implement NOT, AND, OR, XOR, Adders, and MUXes
Standardized low-cost production in 7400 TTL family
disadvantages: Requires multiple gates to form basic OR/AND functions
common_mistakes: Assuming NAND output is 0 when any input is 0 (That is AND logic).
Leaving unneeded NAND gate inputs un-terminated.
quick_notes: Pin 14 is VCC (+5V), Pin 7 is GND.
Tying both inputs of a NAND gate together creates a NOT Inverter.

viva_questions.q: Why is NAND called a Universal Gate?
viva_questions.a: Because any basic or complex digital circuit (NOT, AND, OR, XOR, Adders) can be built using only NAND gates.

viva_questions.q: How do you make an Inverter from a NAND gate?
viva_questions.a: Tie both input pins (A and B) together to form a single input.

interview_questions.q: How many 7400 NAND gates are needed to build a 2-input OR gate?
interview_questions.a: 3 NAND gates (Invert A, Invert B, then pass into third NAND gate: A'+B' = (A·B)' = A+B).
